name: keystone
why: A multi-architecture assembler framework, handy for binary work but more a library than a discovery.

brief.what_it_is: Keystone is a multi-architecture assembler framework, a library you call from C/C++ or from a language binding to turn assembly text into machine-code bytes. The README lists supported targets as Arm, Arm64 (AArch64/Armv8), Ethereum Virtual Machine, Hexagon, Mips, PowerPC, RISC-V, Sparc, SystemZ and X86 (16/32/64-bit). Bindings are listed for Java, Masm, C#, PowerShell, Perl, Python, NodeJS, Ruby, Go, Rust, Haskell, VB6 and OCaml. The brew package also ships a command-line executable named kstool, but the README I read does not describe what it does. The README does not spell out the input and output formats beyond this.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes Keystone as a lightweight, architecture-neutral assembler API, and says it is based on LLVM but goes further, with a separate docs page on what it adds beyond LLVM.

commands_seen.context: From docs/COMPILE.md: builds and installs Keystone through the vcpkg dependency manager in one command, as an alternative to the per-OS compile guides.

brief.install_notes: The README points to docs/COMPILE.md. That page sends you to separate guides: COMPILE-NIX.md for Mac OS X, Linux, BSD, Solaris and other *nix systems; COMPILE-WINDOWS.md for Windows; and COMPILE-WINDOWS-CROSS.md for cross-compiling Windows binaries from Linux. The vcpkg route works on Windows, Linux and macOS. The page also points to C samples in samples/ and Python samples in bindings/python/. I did not open those guides, so I cannot say which build tools or compilers they need. Brew installs the package, but this README does not describe any first-run configuration.
brief.standout: It is LLVM-based but treats the assembler as an architecture-neutral, thread-safe API with many language bindings, rather than a compiler front end. The README's own description of its advantages is that it is lightweight and thread-safe by design.
brief.status: unknown. The README has CI badges for Travis, Semaphore and AppVeyor, but I saw no release date, last-commit date, or changelog. The scout note calls it a library rather than a discovery. The brew package is named keystone.
brief.caveats: Dual license: GPLv2 without the 'any later version' clause, or a commercial royalty-free license for production use (see LICENSE-COM.TXT). The README asks commercial users to contact the authors. Building takes a per-OS guide, and the README says nothing about the kstool executable beyond its name. The README lists no usage commands, so the brief has no usage examples to report.
quotes: Keystone is a lightweight multi-platform, multi-architecture assembler framework.
Keystone is based on LLVM, but it goes much further with a lot more to offer.
